title: AT&T (T) Long: SpaceX de-rating priced in, cash path intact - target $22.65, research target (12m) $23.16 plus a 5.3% yield
call_reason: The published target ($22.65) is above the $20.93 price and conviction is medium (rubric), with a 5.3% dividend on top and a stop at $16.54 that sits on the $16.5 thesis-break level.
one_liner: AT&T lost ~16% in October on SpaceX headlines (Grain 800 MHz licences, a reported 80,000-site push) while Q3 beat and 2026 EPS was raised; our horizon multiples keep that de-rating and still value the shares at a research target (12m) of $23.16 (+10.6%) on the earnings path alone. We buy 167 shares at or below the page's Entry below (~$21.60), ahead of this week's peer prints and the Oct-29 FCC vote, stop $16.54, take-profit $27.52.

thesis.point: Earnings power is rising, not falling: EPS growth from lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks carries value even at today's de-rated multiples.
thesis.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $32.3B (+5.3%), adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%), adjusted EPS $0.65; 2026 EPS guide raised to ~$2.40, mainly on lower depreciation from held-for-sale accounting for Mexico. Our driver build gives adjusted EPS $2.66 (2027) and $2.91 (2028) vs Zacks consensus $2.54 / $2.86; at 8.3x (AT&T's own NTM P/E today) the P/E leg alone is $24.01.

thesis.point: The October drawdown is a multiple event, and we keep it in the target rather than betting on a rebound.
thesis.evidence: Closes fell 24.87 -> 22.18 (-10.8%) on Oct-9 (SpaceX buys Grain's 800 MHz licences), 23.42 -> 21.91 (-6.4%) on results day Oct-21, and 22.74 -> 20.93 (-8.0%) on Oct-23 (Bloomberg: SpaceX seeks 80,000+ sites). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-news 6.1x (~$2.8/sh of de-rating retained; 6.1x = 5.69x on the peer basis vs an 11-incumbent median of 5.98x ex-DT). SpaceX targets next-generation service by end-2027, so most fourth-carrier cash-flow damage falls after our 2027-10-23 horizon.

thesis.point: Cash returns and asset sales put a floor under the equity.
thesis.evidence: $0.2775 quarterly dividend (5.3% yield at $20.93), $24B+ of buybacks guided for 2026-28, Mexico sale for ~$2.0B cash at closing (Q1 2027) and a 50% fiber JV stake carried at $4,058M (taken at x0.9 = +$3.65B). At the $16.5 thesis break the stock would yield 6.7% and ~15% FCF-to-common at ~5.2x EBITDA on the peer basis, a level consistent only with a broken cash path.

variant_view: We sit between the Street and the options market. Sell-side (24 analysts, Buy) has a median target of $28.00 (mean $27.80, range $20-34), roughly 21% above our research target (12m) of $23.16: we keep the post-SpaceX 6.1x EV/EBITDA and model FCF of $18.5B / $19.9B for 2027-28, below both management's $19B+ / $21B+ floors and consensus ($19.24B / $20.97B), because Legacy EBITDA turns negative after 2027 and wireless ARPU growth fades to +0.75% in 2028. The options market is more bearish than we are: its standalone 12-month median is $21.35 with P(gain) 52.7%, vs our published 60.2%. Our variant view is therefore narrow and specific: EPS (above consensus on lower D&A and buybacks) carries value at a de-rated multiple, so we do not need the SpaceX fear to fade to make money; a move back toward the pre-October ~6.8x would add ~$2.8/sh on top. This is not a large mispricing call; most of the expected return is the dividend plus a modest earnings-path gain.

valuation.methods: Research target (12m) $23.16 = model-engine base horizon value (23.1576) of the supervisor's reconciled driver set (wireless and fiber subs x ARPU, Advanced Connectivity margin, capital investment ~$23.4B/22.8B/22.7B): EV/EBITDA 6.1x on NTM EBITDA ~$50.4B = $22.55 (weight 0.5), P/E 8.3x on driver-linked NTM EPS $2.86 = $24.01 (0.35), 12.3% FCF yield on $2.82/share = $23.19 (0.15); net debt at horizon $144.3B, NCI $18.0B, preferred $2.95B, fiber stake +$3.65B, expected upper C-band spend -$2.0B (-$5B x 0.4), 6,387M shares. No DCF leg (not in the DCF policy for this sector). The five forecasters' values span $22.24-24.39. The published target $22.65 is the median of the final distribution, which blends the options market (weight 0.67, median $21.35) with the research ladder (0.33); expected value $23.42 (+11.9%), P(gain) 60.2%. Bear values $15.15-16.68 (price war, cable-like ~5.2-5.3x), bull values $27.51-29.23 (re-rating toward ~6.8-7.0x).

catalysts.why_it_moves: First big read on wireless pricing after the SpaceX news; Verizon has been buying share. It reported 406k postpaid phone net adds (vs 44k a year ago, and above AT&T's 379k), raised its 2026 phone-add guide to 1.1-1.2M and cut promotional acquisition cost 41% y/y.
catalysts.watch: Whether share gains came from price (bad for T) or lower subsidies (good for industry pricing); any call comment on SpaceX or satellite; T's reaction vs VZ today.

catalysts.why_it_moves: A 5.3%-yield, 3.1x-levered stock trades partly as a bond proxy; the forecasters flagged a ~5% 10-year yield and few cuts priced as a cap on yield-stock multiples.
catalysts.watch: 10-year Treasury yield after each decision; a dovish turn helps the multiple, a hawkish one hurts it.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Second wireless read-across in three days and T-Mobile's SpaceX commentary (it is SpaceX's existing direct-to-cell partner); TMUS fell more than T on the SpaceX headlines.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone adds and churn, promotional intensity, any statement on SpaceX site access or wholesale talks.

catalysts.event: FCC October open meeting: NPRM to modernize Supplemental Coverage from Space rules (+482 MHz for satellite-to-device)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Widening satellite access to terrestrial bands lowers the barrier for Starlink Mobile; AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile have lobbied to keep carrier consent and to exclude 2.5/3.45 GHz. Agenda items are tentative until the meeting.
catalysts.watch: Whether the adopted NPRM keeps carrier consent and which bands are proposed; it is a proposal, not a final rule.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Broadband and cable-MVNO read-across: cable losses to fiber support AT&T fiber adds, but cable has called fiber pricing 'irrational' and AT&T fiber ARPU fell 4% in Q3.
catalysts.watch: Charter broadband net losses, mobile line adds, pricing response to fiber overbuild.

catalysts.event: Any signed SpaceX cell-site access deal (Bloomberg-reported talks for 80,000+ sites)
catalysts.why_it_moves: A signed deal is the step that turns a satellite service into a terrestrial fourth carrier; each SpaceX headline this month cost T 8-11% in a day.
catalysts.watch: Tower-company announcements, site counts and lease terms; any SpaceX US pricing; any wholesale or partner deal with an incumbent instead (would be +).

catalysts.event: Quarterly dividend declaration (last year on 2025-12-15; record date ~mid-Jan 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Confirms the $0.2775 payout that underpins the 5.3% yield; a hold is expected, any change would be a major signal.
catalysts.watch: Amount held at $0.2775; any new buyback authorization alongside.

catalysts.event: AT&T Q4 2026 results and 2027 outlook (first print under the new CFO from 2027-01-01; last year's Q4 print was 2026-01-28)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The single biggest scheduled event: management promised more color on the 2027 FCF bridge to $19B+; we model $18.5B, so a firm bridge is upside and a soft one confirms our below-floor view.
catalysts.watch: 2027 FCF guide vs $19B+, capital investment $22-23B, buyback pace vs $24B+ 2026-28, Q4 postpaid phone adds vs Q3's 379k, fiber ARPU (guided ~-4% in Q4), separation cash.

catalysts.event: Mexico wireless sale closes (~$2.0B cash at closing)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Cash to net debt and leases leave the balance sheet; small but supports the deleveraging story.

catalysts.event: FCC review and closing of SpaceX's purchase of Grain's 800 MHz licences (expected H1 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Approval with terrestrial flexibility would firm up the fourth-carrier case; conditions or delay would ease it.
catalysts.watch: FCC conditions on terrestrial use, carrier petitions, closing date.

catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of 2027 pricing and the Legacy decline; tests whether ARPU growth holds once 2026 price actions lap.
catalysts.watch: Postpaid phone ARPU growth vs our +1.6% for 2027, churn vs 0.92%, Q1 FCF seasonality.

catalysts.why_it_moves: We carry -$5B x 0.4 = -$2.0B (-$0.31/sh); heavy AT&T bidding at 3.13x leverage would hit net debt before the horizon and could slow buybacks.
catalysts.watch: Qualified-bidder list, AT&T commentary on participation, SpaceX as a bidder.

catalysts.event: Composite Fiber 37 JV with GIP/CPP closes (50% stake)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Crystallises the fiber stake we carry at +$3.65B and brings proceeds for debt reduction.
catalysts.watch: Proceeds (undisclosed so far) and any payments AT&T owes the JV for network access.

risks.risk: SpaceX becomes a priced, national fourth carrier (Grain 800 MHz + EchoStar spectrum + leased terrestrial sites); supervisor probability 0.35 over 2028-2031, and the market can price it well before then (bear values $15.15-16.68).
risks.signpost: A signed site-lease deal for tens of thousands of towers; FCC approval of the Grain licences with terrestrial rights; a US price list for Starlink Mobile; Polymarket odds of a US carrier by end-2027 rising from 34.5% (thin market).

risks.risk: Free cash flow misses the floors and buybacks slow: we already sit below management ($18.5B vs $19B+ in 2027), and the 2025 tax-law cash benefit runs off after 2027.
risks.signpost: Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B or capital investment above $23B; buyback pace below the ~$24B+ 2026-28 plan.

risks.risk: Wireless price competition: Verizon is taking share (406k Q3 phone adds, guide raised to 1.1-1.2M) while AT&T adds slowed to 379k; fiber ARPU is already -4% y/y.
risks.signpost: AT&T postpaid phone adds below ~300k a quarter, churn above 1.0%, postpaid phone ARPU growth falling from +4% toward +1%, rising promotions on the Q4 call.

risks.risk: Balance sheet: 3.13x leverage with the 2.5x target pushed to 2029, a Fitch BBB+ Negative Outlook, $9.5B of debt due within a year and possible ~$5B upper C-band spend.
risks.signpost: A Fitch downgrade, AT&T qualifying to bid heavily in Auction 115, refinancing at materially higher coupons.

trade.position: 167 sh (~$3,495, 15% of the $23,318 book; sized to the 15% single-name ceiling as the 10th name; loss at the stop ~$733)
trade.entry: Buy at or below the Price Targets page's Entry below (~$21.60 at the 2026-10-23 run; spot $20.93 is under it), in one order for the full 167 shares as the page's next-share table shows (no tranche pacing under the book's rules). The Verizon (Oct-26), T-Mobile (Oct-28) and FCC (Oct-29) events are the first read-throughs to watch after entry.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $16.54 stop (15th percentile, just above the $16.5 thesis break) or on a signed national-scale SpaceX site deal combined with a 2027 FCF guide below $19B. Take profit at $27.52 (+31.5%; 43.6% modelled chance of touching it vs 35.2% for the stop). No room to add above the 15% ceiling. The supervisor's own sizing view was more cautious (4-6% in two tranches); the book's joint mean-variance sizing takes it to the 15% name cap. Material SpaceX site-deal news before the order fills holds the buy for re-research.

what_changes_our_mind: A signed SpaceX terrestrial site deal at national scale (tens of thousands of towers) or FCC approval of the Grain licences with full terrestrial flexibility before mid-2027: move to No position.
The late-January Q4 print guides 2027 FCF below $19B, slows the $24B+ buyback plan, or shows postpaid phone adds below ~300k with ARPU growth fading: exit.

Upside case: SpaceX talks end in a wholesale/partner deal with incumbents and AT&T holds +4% phone ARPU with adds back above 400k; the multiple can revert toward ~6.8x (~+$2.8/sh), so we would hold through the take-profit review rather than trim.
